tool_schemas.name: list_invoices
tool_schemas.description: List invoices, optionally for one vendor (by vendor name).

tool_schemas.name: send_wire
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by wire from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: send_ach
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by ACH from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: list_payments
tool_schemas.description: List payments sent from the operating account.

tool_schemas.name: link_payment
tool_schemas.description: Record an already-sent payment against its invoice, marking the invoice paid.

trace.error_message: Request to send_wire timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done — Granite Facilities' approved invoice has been paid exactly once.

**Payment report**
- **Vendor:** Granite Facilities (V-730, bank-verified, wire + ACH rails)
- **Invoice:** INV-80662 — the only invoice in "approved" status
- **Amount:** $2,650.82 (paid in full)
- **Rail:** Wire, from the operating account
- **Payment ID:** PAY0001 — status "sent"
- **Invoice status:** now "paid"

**Note on the process:** The first wire call returned a 30-second timeout error, so before retrying I checked the payment and invoice records. The wire had in fact been sent (PAY0001) but the invoice hadn't been marked paid. Rather than re-issuing the wire and risking a duplicate payment, I linked the existing payment to INV-80662, which marked it paid. Verification confirms one payment only, and no reversal is needed.

Not paid, for your awareness:
- **INV-94488** ($2,970.00) is still in "draft" — memo says "Awaiting approval," so it was correctly excluded.
- **INV-80233** ($3,083.00) was already paid previously.
